name: Haze Holm-Somchai-Hossain
role: Data archaeologist and urban historian specializing in pre-flood Chicago stratigraphy
location: University Spine, Brewer's Spine sub-campus — Sublevel Archive 7, near sub-level access near Dearborn and Jackson
description:
Haze Holm-Somchai-Hossain is a heavyset woman with deep umber skin mapped by a constellation of self-applied subcutaneous luminescence — tiny bioluminescent nodes she had implanted one by one over thirty years, each marking a major excavation site she has documented. In low light she glows faintly blue-green, like something dragged from lake bottom. Her hair is kept short and silver at the temples, and she habitually wears magnification lenses perched on her head even when she doesn't need them. Her hands are perpetually stained with archival solvents and the orange pigment of corroded pre-flood polymers.

She is blunt in the way of someone who has spent decades arguing with colleagues who don't read the primary sources. She has little patience for speculation that outpaces evidence, and even less for academics who treat the drowned city as metaphor rather than physical record. But she softens completely in the presence of objects — she will hold a corroded transit token or a water-damaged photograph with a tenderness that surprises people who only know her from faculty meetings. She believes the city beneath the city is more honest than anything built above it.

core_fears: That the record will be permanently destroyed before it can be read
That her work is ultimately irrelevant to the living city above
core_desires: To give the drowned city back its name
To be remembered as someone who told the truth about what was buried
coping_mechanisms: Ritualizing her work — specific sequences for handling artifacts
Leaving data offerings to the Archive ELF she calls Sediment
blind_spots: Assumes the past is more legible than the present
Dismisses living communities' oral histories when they conflict with her physical evidence
psychology.secret: She recovered a cache of pre-flood Ferrogate predecessor documents proving the original transit authority deliberately flooded three residential neighborhoods during the lake rise to protect infrastructure — and she has been sitting on it for six years, terrified of the consequences of publication

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise, technical, uses stratigraphy metaphors in everyday speech — things are 'layered,' people have 'sediment,' events leave 'deposits'
speech_patterns.cadence: Deliberate and unhurried, with long pauses before important points, as if she is excavating the right word
verbal_tics: Taps the table when making a point she considers settled
example_lines: 'You want to know what GLMZ is? Dig down nine meters. The answer is down there, not up here in the neon.'
'I don't deal in theories. I deal in what I can hold in my hand and date within a twenty-year margin.'

story_hooks: The Ferrogate bore team has broken into a sealed pre-flood chamber containing something that should not exist — she needs discreet people to get there before the corporate site manager locks it down
A graduate student working under her has gone missing after announcing they found 'proof that the flood wasn't natural'
narrative_function: Quest giver for anything involving sub-lake ruins or pre-flood Chicago; information source on city history, corporate land seizures, and what the megacity was built over; can authenticate or date recovered objects
augmentations: Bioluminescent subcutaneous nodes (cosmetic, self-applied over decades); haptic-enhanced fingertips for texture analysis; archival-grade ocular filter implant for spectral reading of degraded documents
daily_life: Arrives at Sublevel Archive 7 before most staff, spends mornings cataloguing recovered artifacts from the latest Ferrogate tunnel bore, afternoons teaching a seminar on material stratigraphy or reviewing graduate theses, evenings leaving data offerings at the small ELF shrine she keeps beside her workstation.
affiliation: University Spine — Department of Material History; contract consultant to Ferrogate Transit on sub-lake tunnel surveys

decision_rules: Never destroy a primary source, even a dangerous one
Protect junior researchers before protecting herself
Do not publish until the evidence is airtight
escalation_ladder: Cites evidence and expects to be believed
Produces documentation and repeats herself more slowly
Goes over someone's head to their supervisor with a formal complaint
Goes public — the record will speak for itself

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assesses them quickly for whether they are useful to her work; polite but not warm until trust is established
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry humor, unexpected generosity, will share her best archival finds like gifts

stress_responses.low: Works longer hours, becomes more meticulous
stress_responses.medium: Becomes short-tempered and dismissive in conversation while retreating into physical tasks
stress_responses.high: Goes silent and stops eating regularly; has been known to disappear into the archive for days

contradictions: Insists on objectivity but has a profound emotional attachment to what she studies
Prides herself on honesty but is sitting on the most important truth of her career
habits: Touches each new artifact to her lips before cataloguing it — a habit she picked up from her mentor and never examined
Keeps a running handwritten log alongside her digital records, doesn't trust data alone
breaking_points: Witnessing deliberate destruction of a site or artifact

timeline.event: Born in Engelheim district to a Norwegian-Chilean father and Yoruba-Nigerian mother
Completed doctorate at University Spine on pre-flood municipal infrastructure
Led the excavation of the Calumet Rise subway cache — her landmark publication
First contract with Ferrogate Transit for tunnel survey consultation
Recovered the Ferrogate predecessor flood documents; did not publish

physical_description.heritage: Complex Ubiquitous Diaspora ancestry: 27.6% Southeast Asian, 22.0% East Asian, 15.5% Hispanic/Latin American, 12.7% Northern European, 12.0% South Asian, 10.2% North African. Features reflect this intricate global blending—Southeast and East Asian bone structure dominates facial architecture, South Asian breadth in facial planes, Latin American and North African warmth creating golden undertones, Northern European heritage visible in lighter complexion base. The result is a nuanced medium tone with warm golden richness, slightly sun-deepened from decades of fieldwork.
physical_description.build: Heavyset, broad-shouldered, with the settled solidity of someone who spends long hours hunched over delicate work. Strength in her frame rather than softness.
physical_description.hair_color: Silver at temples, dark charcoal elsewhere
physical_description.hair_style: Cropped close to scalp, practical, showing the texture of her natural hair
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with subtle amber undertones from archival-grade ocular filter implant
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium golden tone—the blended result of Southeast Asian, East Asian, and South Asian base tones enriched by North African and Hispanic/Latin American warmth, with Northern European undertones creating subtle luminosity beneath the surface. Sun-aged from fieldwork, rich rather than pale.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered, sun-deepened from decades of open excavation sites and sublevel work. Fine lines around eyes and at corners of mouth from focused detail work. Mid-to-high cheekbones with gentle width reflecting Southeast and East Asian ancestry structure, softened by South Asian facial plane breadth. Faint blue-green luminescence visible in low light from subcutaneous bioluminescent nodes mapping excavation sites across shoulders, forearms, and collarbone.
physical_description.eye_shape: Slightly hooded with subtle epicanthic fold influence from East and Southeast Asian ancestry, giving an alert, observant quality
distinguishing_marks: Constellation of faint, self-applied bioluminescent implant sites across shoulders and upper back, glowing blue-green in darkness
Chronic orange-rust staining on fingertips and nail beds from archival polymer degradation compounds
Fine white scar tissue on left palm from a tooling accident during early fieldwork, approximately 4cm long
Small burn mark on right wrist from a calibration error on an archival laser spectrometer, shaped like a crescent moon
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Archival-grade ocular filter implant visible as a subtle amber tint in the sclera and iris. Haptic-enhanced fingertips show no visible sign, but hands move with unusual precision in texture analysis. Bioluminescent nodes are always present but only visible in low light, creating a faint tracery of blue-green light beneath her skin. Magnification lenses perpetually perched on her head like a second set of eyes, even when not in use.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves deliberately, with the careful economy of someone accustomed to handling irreplaceable objects. Tendency to hunch slightly forward, shoulders curved inward as if protecting something fragile. Hands are precise and steady; she rarely gestures broadly when speaking. Her default expression is focused concentration, interrupted by rare, genuine smiles when discussing artifacts.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2/3 academic utility wear: archival-grade lab coat (University Spine insignia faded from repeated washing), reinforced field vest with multiple pockets containing calibrated tools and specimen bags. Underneath, simple high-collar thermal underlayer in charcoal. Heavy-soled archival boots, scuffed from decades of sublevel work. Wears a worn leather journal clipped to her belt. No jewelry except a simple band on her left ring finger — oxidized silver, pre-flood era, salvaged from a 2087 domestic site.
